goal: Find out whether the roughly 3,000 words of beau-mode's SKILL.md that beau-agent loads before any work help or distract, compared with a slim router that restates the task, picks a playbook and reads only that playbook and the principles it names, so the always-on text is cut only if the slim router does as well (R43).
changed: ROADMAP R43 is done with a keep recommendation: the slim arm fell outside the noise band on scope and reply.

The change folder holds the eval's report, the rubric and rules written before judging, the 8 tasks, the slim arm's text, the judge's per-task verdicts, the computed win shares, a per-run table and the harness that ran it.

claims.claim: The slim arm holds on cause, fix and proof and does not hold on scope (0.344 against a band of 0) or reply (0.281 against a band of 0.125), so the pre-registered rule says keep.
claims.check: score.py over the 8 judge verdicts, all status ok, against the rule in prereg.md
claims.remaining: 8 tasks and one identical-run pair for the band; the judge has beau-mode loaded through cursor-agent's user rules; label positions were not balanced.

claims.claim: The full arm adds 7,505 tokens to the system prompt and the slim arm 2,169, and cost per run was $0.36 for full and $0.38 for slim.
claims.check: tok.py: one-word claude -p replies on Sonnet with each arm and with none; total_cost_usd per run from the transcripts
claims.remaining: Sonnet in claude -p only; other tools and models were not run.

claims.claim: The full arm opened its playbook in 10 of 16 runs and the slim arm in 8 of 8; no run opened a principle file.
claims.check: Read tool and shell calls touching the kit's playbooks and principles, counted from each run's stream-json transcript
claims.remaining: Why the full arm skips its playbook is inferred, not tested.

claims.claim: The merged PRs' own new tests can separate the arms.
claims.check: truth.py ran them for t3, t7 and t8 against the base and every candidate
claims.remaining: They fail on the unmodified base and on nearly every candidate because they test the merged design, so they cannot stand in for the judge.

next.item: R13's beau-mode comparison reuses these tasks, harness and full runs
next.why_now: R43 was to run first so R13 could reuse its tasks, and R42 already reuses them.
next.impact: R13 starts with 8 tasks, a harness and a noise band instead of building them, which makes its runs cheap.

next.item: Test why the full arm skips its playbook in 6 of 16 runs, for example by repeating step 2 at the end of SKILL.md
next.why_now: It is the one place this eval shows the always-on text distracting, and the tasks and harness are ready.
next.impact: Agents that skip the playbook skip its proof and gate steps. If a moved step 2 gets every run to open its playbook, beau-agent's work gets those checks every time.

release.none: An eval and its record; no plugin or skill text changed.
